network.comment: Layer 1 allow: stable NetBird FQDN for proxy-peer. Layer 2 (NetBird route enable/disable on mitmproxy's wt0) controls whether the connection actually succeeds.

_layer1_mesh_notes: Layer 1 (mitmproxy allow/deny) determines whether mitmproxy attempts to forward
a request. Layer 2 (NetBird Routes API, managed by capability-runtime) determines
whether the destination is reachable via mitmproxy's wt0 mesh interface.
For arbitrary mesh CIDRs leased dynamically, add a coarse Layer 1 rule:
or per-peer FQDN rules using the NetBird mesh DNS domain:
A Layer 1 allow is a necessary but not sufficient condition for reachability.
If the Layer 2 NetBird route is revoked, the connection will time out after
mitmproxy attempts to forward it (TCP timeout, no route on wt0). This is
intentional: Layer 1 blocks immediately; Layer 2 blocks post-mitmproxy.
